verdictStatement: All seven claimed repairs are real and I verified each against the frozen findings' own required-repair text rather than against the repair log's summary of them. The four Codex blockers are genuinely closed: the selector language is now a closed tagged union owned by this contract with normalization, endpoint order and inclusivity, wildcard and empty-set rejection, equality and serialization; SONAME-ABI is removed from every classMap and demoted to an additional compatibility selector that is 'never sole authenticity evidence for any class, including libc'; the declared signed shape is the exhaustive four-field entry with a closed FIXED/FORBIDDEN environment map that forbids PATH and loader substitution by default and refuses any lookup step touching a forbidden or unnamed variable; and the loader-trace boundary is requantified over every actual attempt whether or not declared, with an independent capture sensor that may not declare its own output complete. Both Codex SHOULD-FIX items and my own blocker are closed too — the carrier now has one DR-101 author with a carrier-absent G22 block, and the eight ownerArtifact designations I objected to are gone with the indefinite reservation restored, including the refusal to name a replacement owner. What withholds acceptance is that those eight removals are the one part of the delta the closed roster does not name, which makes the roster's own closure sentence false on the axis both v3 reviewers already flagged.

repairVerification.finding: PTCB-V3-B1 — selectorGrammar named fields but defined neither selector
repairVerification.status: REPAIRED — FULLY, against every element Codex enumerated
repairVerification.detail: selectorGrammar now owns a closed tagged union. EXACT-BUILD carries a canonical identifier, Unicode NFC plus whitespace-trim normalization, byte-exact equality, and wildcard and empty rejection. CLOSED-RANGE carries the same identifier domain, inclusive endpoints with the platform-published total order, per-endpoint normalization, wildcard rejection, an empty-set rule ('lower greater than upper … is empty and refuses'), and structural equality. Serialization is 'exactly one tag object', unrecognized tags refuse, and the packet 'MUST NOT mint a third range semantics'. Filesystem identity is a canonical identifier enum with an other:<digest-bound-fstype-token> escape, byte-exact equality, and wildcard, empty and or-join rejection. Codex asked for domain/order, normalization, wildcard/empty rejection, equality and serialization; all five are present for both selectors.

repairVerification.finding: PTCB-V3-B2 — SONAME-ABI preserved same-label libc substitution
repairVerification.detail: In v3 the libc classMap was [PLATFORM-ATTESTED, SONAME-ABI], so a label-only tag could stand as sole identity. In v4 libc is [PLATFORM-ATTESTED, DIGEST-BOUND] and SONAME-ABI appears in no classMap entry at all — I checked all eight classes. A different object publishing the same labels is not the same member.' comparison adds 'it never replaces it' and drops v3's 'unless the population packet defines a closed range form' escape, binding exactness to selectorGrammar instead.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the selector grammar was defined loosely enough for a packet to mint range semantics. Both tags are closed, serialization admits exactly one tag object, and the packet is barred from a third semantics in two places.
That SONAME-ABI survives as sufficient identity somewhere. It appears in no classMap entry across all eight classes and carries an explicit notSufficient.
That naming a loader variable still makes substitution lawful. The default is FORBIDDEN, unnamed is FORBIDDEN, and a named variable without a fixed value is called out as not lawful.
That the completeness proof can still be self-asserted. The sensor must be independent of the process under test and the recorder is forbidden to declare its own output complete.
That the carrier still has two owners. One author is named and DR-103's relation is consumption.
That the ownerArtifact repair substituted a different designation. It designates nothing and says choosing an owner is a separate decision.
That a per-OS table was quietly populated while the grammar was being written. All four stems remain RESERVED.
coordinatorNote: This is the strongest generation in this lineage by a wide margin. Four blockers, two SHOULD-FIX items and my own blocker are all genuinely closed, and I checked each against the frozen findings' own required-repair text rather than the repair log's paraphrase — the B2 fix in particular is verifiable structurally, since SONAME-ABI now appears in no classMap at all rather than merely being annotated. The CLAUDE-V3-B1 repair also did the harder half of what I asked: it removed the designation without substituting another one, which is the restraint I flagged as the point of the finding. What stops acceptance is narrow and mechanical. The eight ownerArtifact deletions that constitute that very repair are the only part of a 46-path delta the closed roster does not name, and because the roster names two other children of the same parent by sub-path, the omission is not covered by implication. The closure sentence is therefore false, on precisely the axis both v3 reviewers independently raised and which PTCB-V3-S2 asked to be fixed by refreezing and remeasuring the diff. The change is disclosed in the repair log, so this is completeness rather than concealment, and the fix is to add one path to the roster with no text change anywhere else. DR-126 stays OPEN, no per-OS table is populated, no D-096 (A) grant is minted, and nothing here marks the row SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
